1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 f5 4.Nc3 fxe4 5..strategy: Recaptures with the knight, which sits strongly on e4 and eyes d6 and f6. White keeps a lead in development, and Black must choose how to challenge the knight.

Challenges the knight with a developing move and avoids the forcing lines of the pawn thrust. Black plays for activity and the bishop pair, usually at the cost of the e5 pawn; it is now often considered the main line.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 f5 4.Nc3 fxe4 5..name: Ruy Lopez: Schliemann Defence, Tartakower Variation
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 f5 4.Nc3 fxe4 5..background: 5...Nf6 has increased in popularity to the point that it is now often considered the main line after 4.Nc3. Teimour Radjabov, who plays the gambit regularly, prefers it.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 f5 4.Nc3 fxe4 5..strategy: Challenges the knight with a pawn and builds a classical centre, leading to well-analysed lines of the gambit. A retreat by the knight would leave Black doing well, but White has a sharp sacrifice in reply, and Black has scored poorly in those lines.

A quiet developing move that prepares to castle but does not challenge the strong knight on e4, and e5 depends on the c6 knight alone. It avoids the sharp pawn lines, yet Black has given White a free hand.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 f5 4.Nc3 fxe4 5..name: Ruy Lopez: Schliemann Defence, Kostić Defence
